title: Throughput fidelity bands and proportional crediting playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable, auditor-friendly framework that maps observed dedicated-capacity degradation into proportionate customer credits while preserving operational guardrails. This ticket codifies measurement windows, fidelity bands (Gold / Silver / Bronze), autoscaler interlock behavior during SLA events, and standardized contract clause language for new Dedicated agreements.

Scope: SLA definitions for committed throughput (tokens per minute or requests per second depending on customer billing), sliding error budget/windowing rules, credit computation examples, notice and remediation timelines, and how autoscaling events interact with crediting (autoscaler interlock). Excludes pricing negotiation language and legal contract signature templates (handled in parallel).

Goals:
- Produce a concise SLA clause and annex to include in Dedicated contracts that customers and sales can sign off on.
- Provide operational measurement definitions (metrics, aggregation, and telemetry sources) to enable automated credit computation.
- Define a playbook for fault diagnosis, short-term remediation, and credit arbitration.
- Ensure alignment between product, infra, reliability, and legal on Escalation/Notice windows.
acceptance_criteria: Draft SLA clause (plain-English + normative definitions) that can be embedded into Dedicated contracts and reviewed by legal.
Telemetry spec (metric names, consumer of source, aggregation window, and fallback sources) for automated credit calculation implemented by Observability team.
Credit computation examples with numeric scenarios for Gold/Silver/Bronze bands and edge cases (partial hour failures, bursty load).
Operational playbook describing detection -> customer notice -> remediation -> credit issuance workflow including timing and stakeholders.
Autoscaler interlock behavior documented: when autoscale triggers pause credit accrual, when it doesn't, and how manual overrides are recorded.
Review and sign-off from Legal, Reliability Engineering, and Sales Engineering documented in ticket comments.
decisions: Use sliding 60-minute window sampled at 1-minute granularity for primary throughput measurement (fallback to 5-minute aggregated windows if minute level telemetry is missing).

Measure customer entitlement as 'committed tokens per minute' (CTPM) for token-billed customers and 'committed requests per minute' (CRPM) for request-billed customers. Contracts will include the chosen unit per customer.
Establish three fidelity bands with corresponding credit rates: Gold (>=98% of CTPM, 0% credit), Silver (95-98%, prorated credits), Bronze (<95%, capped credits plus remediation plan).
Credit calculation will be proportional to the fractional shortfall over the measurement window with a maximum cap per billing period to limit financial exposure. Example formula included in annex.
notes: We purposely avoid single-point outages being treated the same as sustained degradation; credits are calculated over sliding windows to avoid outsized crediting for short blips.

Autoscaler interlock: if autoscaler was paused for customer-directed maintenance or a scheduled migration (documented via maintenance API), that downtime is excluded from credit windows when notice was provided ahead of time.
Edge case: if customer traffic is so low that measurement noise dominates, use absolute token threshold floor to avoid over-crediting (e.g., minimum comparison volume of 10k tokens per 60 minutes).
Legal wants a short plain-English clause and a separate technical annex for measurement definitions — both will be delivered with this ticket.
contract_clause_snippet: Service Commitment: Redwood Inference will make best efforts to provide the Committed Throughput specified in Customer's Dedicated agreement. Committed Throughput shall be measured against the Customer's contractual unit (Committed Tokens Per Minute or Committed Requests Per Minute) using Redwood's monitoring pipeline over sliding 60-minute windows sampled at 1-minute granularity. If observed throughput falls below 95% of the Committed Throughput for any sliding 60-minute window, Customer will be eligible for credits computed in accordance with the Credit Annex. Credits are calculated proportionally to the measured shortfall subject to the maximum credit cap described in the Credit Annex. Credits constitute Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for throughput degradation except as otherwise agreed in writing.
credit_annex_summary: Measurement: primary metric = customer_served_unit_per_minute (1-min samples) aggregated into sliding 60-minute windows. Shortfall fraction = max(0, 1 - observed/committed) per window. Credit rate bands: Gold (observed >=0.98*committed) => 0% credit; Silver (0.95 <= observed < 0.98) => prorated credit = shortfall_fraction * 0.5 * billing_amount_for_window; Bronze (observed <0.95) => prorated credit = shortfall_fraction * billing_amount_for_window subject to monthly cap of 15% of monthly Dedicated fee. Example: Committed = 120k tokens/min, observed = 108k => shortfall_fraction=0.1 => if Silver/Bronze logic applies, compute prorated credit per annex. Credits issued after verification and dispute window.
measurement_spec: Metric name(s): dedicated.customer_served_tokens_per_minute OR dedicated.customer_served_requests_per_minute. Primary source: metrics pipeline (prometheus -> metrics-aggregator -> billing-ledger). Aggregation: sliding window of 60 minutes at 1-minute resolution; fallback to 5-minute resolution if minute-granularity missing. Percentiles: use 95th percentile across the 60 one-minute samples to reduce noise. Missing data policy: if >10% of samples in window are missing, mark window as 'insufficient' and escalate to on-call for manual reconciliation before crediting.
autoscale_interlock_policy: If an autoscale action (automatic or recommendation) was taken by Redwood during a degradation window, credits are calculated normally. If customer-initiated autoscaler pause or manual capacity release is recorded via the maintenance API with prior notice, those intervals are excluded from credit eligibility. Manual overrides are logged and audited; to avoid disputes, require a maintenance ticket or API event with at least 30 minutes notice for exclusion. If autoscaler caused insufficient capacity due to throttling bug (root cause attribution to Redwood), incident response playbook applies and credits may be escalated beyond formula.
escalation_and_notice: Detection -> 15 minute automated customer notification (passive status: 'we detected degraded serve for your Dedicated instance, we're investigating') -> 2-hour operations update if unresolved -> 24-hour remediation plan and credit estimate or final credit issuance timeline. Credit issuance occurs after validation (automated + 24-hour dispute window) and is reflected on the following billing statement unless otherwise agreed. Legal and Customer Success are notified for any credits >5% of monthly bill prior to issuance.
examples: Scenario A (brief blip): Committed=100k tpm, observed 1-minute drop to 80k for 2 minutes within a 60-min window, the 95th percentile across the 60 samples remains >=98k => Gold band, no credit.

Scenario B (sustained partial degradation): Committed=200k tpm, observed sustained 180k across 60-min sliding window => observed/committed=0.9 => shortfall_fraction=0.1 -> falls into Bronze band -> credit = shortfall_fraction * billing_amount_for_window subject to monthly cap and verification.
Scenario C (autoscaler pause for maintenance): Customer paused autoscaler via maintenance API with 1-hour scheduled window; observed shortfall during that window is excluded from credit computation.
open_questions: Should credits for Silver band scale linearly with shortfall_fraction or apply a fixed multiplier (we propose 0.5x to partially share risk)?
Do we want to surface raw per-minute samples to customers via a portal or provide only aggregate verification reports?
How should credits interact with usage-based discounts that are tiered by volume? Do credits reduce future committed capacity or only billing amounts?
